answer: Non-kin attestation quorums resist sybils: an identity counts only once enough established, UNRELATED peers vouch for it, and self-referential rings are discounted. A fake cluster is a closed island vouching only for itself on its own terrace, earning nothing — it draws no genuine edges across the delta to real peers. Honest identities gather many independent vouches; a ring has only its own, so the counting rule starves it.
